plain: Payment to make up for a loss or to protect from one.

webster.text: The act of indemnifying, saving harmless, or securing against loss, damage or penalty.

example.quote: which provides that none shall be taken directly even for public use without indemnification to the owner, and yet directly violates the property which individuals have in their opinions, their religion, their persons, and their faculties;
example.cite: James Madison, Property, National Gazette, Mar. 29, 1792
